items.title: Edit Discovery in Human-AI Interactions
items.abstract: Human-AI interactions are becoming a rich source of data for improving AI systems: while many model responses are already satisfactory, others expose failures that could become valuable supervision if identified and corrected. We study this setting through the notion of an editor: a more capable evaluation process that can inspect a response and either confirm it or modify it, but whose invocation is costly. The editor may be a human expert, a stronger AI system, or the same model equipped with additional computation, context, tools, or information. The key challenge is to decide which interactions to send to the editor before knowing whether an edit will actually be made, since invoking the editor itself consumes limited resources such as expert time, inference cost, latency, or tool-use overhead. We formulate this problem as Edit Discovery Optimization (EDO), which seeks to minimize edit opportunities missed among skipped interactions while controlling unnecessary confirmations and respecting an editor-cost budget. We characterize the population-optimal policy and show that it takes the form of a cost-adjusted threshold on the posterior probability of an edit. Building on this structure, we develop EDIT (Edit Discovery via Iterative Thresholding), an online algorithm for the partial-feedback setting in which edit labels are revealed only for selected interactions. EDIT combines an adaptive edit score, a confirmation-control threshold, and a cost-aware selection rule; it satisfies the editor budget at every round and controls the average confirmation rate up to a vanishing finite-horizon term, without distributional assumptions on the interaction stream. Across four reasoning and factual question-answering benchmarks, EDIT achieves a better trade-off between editor cost, Type-I error, and Type-II error than direct LLM-based batch selection.

items.title: EEG-biometric authentication system using multi-paradigm neurophysiological measurements and artificial intelligence
items.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) provides a promising physiological modality for biometric authentication due to its inherent neural uniqueness and resistance to spoofing attacks. However, reliable EEG-based authentication remains challenging because brain signals are highly non-stationary and vary across cognitive states. To address this limitation, this study proposes a multi-paradigm neurophysiological measurement protocol designed to capture stable subject-specific EEG signatures across diverse brain conditions. EEG signals were recorded from participants during six complementary paradigms, including eyes-open and eyes-closed resting states, left and right-hand motor tasks, working-memory encoding, steady-state visual evoked potentials (SSVEP), and steady-state auditory evoked potentials (SSAEP). The recorded signals were preprocessed and segmented into 2-s epochs with 50% overlap. We extracted 28 quantitative descriptors per channel from time, frequency, time-frequency, and nonlinear domains. These descriptors were used to evaluate several decision models, including Mahalanobis distance-based template matching, logistic regression (LR), support vector machine, random forest, and a one-dimensional convolutional neural network. The performance of the proposed measurement system was analyzed under both single-paradigm and multi-paradigm configurations using cross-session validation. Experimental results show that the multi-paradigm measurement protocol reduces the equal error rate (EER) by 2% compared with single-paradigm systems. The LR decision model achieved the best performance with an EER of 1.6% (95% confidence interval: 1.48−1.73), with false rejection rates of 2.06% and 9.01% at false acceptance rates of 1% and 0.1%, respectively. Feature analysis indicated that Hjorth mobility and Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients derived from fronto-central cortical channels provide the most reliable neural identity descriptors. These results demonstrate that multi-paradigm EEG acquisition improves the stability of neural measurements across cognitive states and enables reliable biometric authentication in dynamic conditions.

items.title: Effect of Acoustic Congruency in Binaural Audio on the Film-Viewing Experience
items.abstract: Binaural audio provides an accessible alternative to multi-loudspeaker reproduction. However, However, binaural reproduction often involves a mismatch between the acoustics of the simulated virtual room and the listener’s physical environment, which can compromise auditory distance perception and plausibility, a phenomenon known as the room divergence effect. This study investigated whether such mismatch influences immersive experience during film viewing and which auditory perceptual factors are associated with immersion. Sixty-eight participants watched an excerpt from Dune: Part One (2021) using binaurally rendered multichannel audio under acoustically convergent and divergent conditions in a critical listening room and a domestic living room. Immersion was assessed using the Film Immersive Experience Questionnaire alongside an exploratory Binaural Audio Experience Questionnaire. Although room divergence produced perceptually salient differences, it did not significantly affect overall immersive experience. However, specific immersion dimensions, particularly Transportation, were more closely associated with localization and listener envelopment than with auditory distance and externalization.

items.title: Effectiveness of a hospital intelligent financial system based on AI and RPA
items.abstract: Background Hospital financial management is facing ongoing challenges. Although artificial intelligence (AI) and robotic process automation (RPA) have shown their potential, there is still a lack of empirical evidence of the effectiveness of the integration of the two in the financial operations of hospitals. This study aims to evaluate the application effect of a set of an AI-RPA integrated intelligent financial system in a large hospital in China. Methods This single-center, non-randomized, uncontrolled before-and-after study was carried out in a large tertiary A general hospital in China from January to December 2025. As an intervention, the intelligent AI-RPA financial system launched in June 2025 consists of four levels: data governance, business processing, technology application and risk control. The study compared the 6 months before the system was launched and the 6 months after the system was launched, in terms of operational efficiency (daily data collection time, report generation time, and automated processing time per transaction), data quality and risk control (data docking success rate, data entry error rate, logical conflict correction rate, and risk prediction accuracy for medical insurance violations) and health-care staff satisfaction. Results After the system went online, the daily data collection time was shortened from 132.5 to 18.6 min ( P < 0.001); the report generation time was shortened from 58.4 to 5.8 min ( P < 0.001); the automated processing time of each transaction was reduced from 3.5 to 1.9 s ( P < 0.001). Data interfacing success rate increased from 94.2 to 99.7%, data entry error rate dropped from 3.5 to 0.6%, logic conflict correction rate rose from 78.1 to 98.5%, and risk prediction accuracy for insurance violations improved from 72.1 to 89.3%. Total staff satisfaction score improved from 30.1 to 43.1 ( P < 0.001). Conclusion This study provides preliminary empirical evidence that the AI-RPA integrated intelligent financial system was associated with improvements in operational efficiency, data quality, risk control, and user satisfaction in a large Chinese hospital.

items.title: Effectiveness of Vestibular Rehabilitation for Oculomotor Symptoms and Disorientation in Individuals With Cybersickness: A Randomized Controlled Trial
items.abstract: BackgroundCybersickness is characterized by oculomotor symptoms and disorientation during prolonged screen or virtual reality exposure.The effectiveness of vestibular rehabilitation for these symptoms remains unclear. MethodsThis two-group randomized controlled trial included 50 adults aged 30-50 years with self-reported cybersickness and more than 12 hours of daily screen exposure.Participants were randomly assigned to a vestibular rehabilitation group (n = 25) or a control group (n = 25).The intervention group performed a structured Cawthorne-Cooksey-based vestibular rehabilitation program for 20 minutes per day, six days per week, for six weeks.The control group received ergonomic and screen-hygiene advice.Oculomotor symptoms and disorientation were assessed using the Simulator Sickness Questionnaire (SSQ) at baseline and six weeks. ResultsAll 50 participants completed the study.Baseline SSQ scores were comparable between groups.At six weeks, the vestibular rehabilitation group demonstrated greater reductions in oculomotor symptoms than the control group (11.3 ± 3.7 vs. 4.2 ± 3.3; between-group difference, 7.1 points; 95% CI, 5.3-8.9;p < 0.001).Similarly, disorientation scores decreased more in the vestibular rehabilitation group than in the control group (14.3 ± 5.0 vs. 5.3 ± 4.1; between-group difference, 9.0 points; 95% CI, 6.6-11.4;p < 0.001). ConclusionsA six-week structured vestibular rehabilitation program produced greater reductions in oculomotor symptoms and disorientation associated with cybersickness than ergonomic and screen-hygiene advice alone.These findings support further investigation of vestibular rehabilitation as a nonpharmacological approach for cybersickness.

items.title: EFL Learner Engagement With CALL
items.abstract: This mixed-methods study investigated Omani EFL university students' engagement, motivation, and perceptions of the Spark digital platform in a blended learning context. Using Self-Determination Theory (SDT), the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), and the Motivated Strategies for Learning Questionnaire (MSLQ) frameworks, the study analyzed survey data, platform analytics, and focus group discussions from 100 students. The results showed that extrinsic, grade-oriented motivation mainly led to moderate engagement. Although analytics suggested high activity, qualitative findings revealed frustration, redundancy, and time pressure. Students reported moderate levels of satisfaction. The study identifies an engagement-compliance paradox, where observable use masks low intrinsic motivation, and recommends a shift to structured in-class use, targeted curriculum alignment, and AI-powered feedback to achieve meaningful and sustained learner engagement.

items.title: El Impacto del Liderazgo Transformacional en la Practica Docente: Un Estudio Comparativo de Escuelas Publicas en Ecuador y Escuelas Privadas K12 en China
items.abstract: This essay comparatively analyzes the implementation of transformational leadership in two distinct educational contexts: the Adolfo Jurado Gonz?lez Basic Education School in Ecuador and private K12 schools in China. Through the analysis of Tomal?'s (2025) thesis and Hou, Ahmad, and Zhao's (2024) systematic review, the similarities and differences in applied theoretical models, leadership dimensions, challenges faced, and results obtained in both countries are examined. Both contexts share the adoption of Bass's (1985) model as the fundamental theoretical basis, confirming the positive impact of transformational leadership on teaching practice, intrinsic motivation, and pedagogical innovation. However, while Ecuador focuses on Bass's four classic dimensions (idealized influence, inspirational motivation, intellectual stimulation, and individualized consideration) within a public system focused on educational equity, China diversifies its theoretical approach by incorporating the models of Kouzes and Posner (2006), Bennis and Nanus (1985), and Leithwood and Sun (2012), adapting to a massive and highly competitive private education market. The identified challenges reveal convergences in communication problems, training, and resistance to change, but also significant differences: Ecuador faces technological gaps and economic resource limitations, while China struggles with the cultural adaptation of Western theories, clarification of roles between management and leadership, and demographic pressures. Methodologically, Ecuador uses a quantitative empirical approach with primary data from a specific school, while China employs a systematic literature review with national scope. Results in Ecuador show high levels of teacher satisfaction (91% trust and respect, 100% commitment), while China emphasizes the need to develop culturally adapted theoretical frameworks of its own. Recommendations from both studies converge on the importance of continuous training and feedback, but diverge in that Ecuador prioritizes practical mechanisms coordinated with existing institutions, while China seeks to build specific theories and strategies for its context. The essay concludes that transformational leadership, although universal in its fundamental principles, requires significant contextual adaptations to be effective in educational realities as diverse as those of Ecuador and China.

items.title: EliteReplay: Preserving Diverse Solutions in RL Post-Training via Quality-Diversity Search
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning has become a common post-training technique to improve the accuracy of LLMs on verifiable tasks. However, such training can narrow the set of solutions the model can produce. Several approaches have attempted to address this behavior-sharpening effect, but they often optimize metrics that do not reflect the diversity of correct solutions. Ideally, we want a model that can produce multiple good solutions, not only a single reliable one. We propose EliteReplay, a post-training recipe that pairs GRPO with an "elite" archive built by quality-diversity search. Before training, we use the frozen base model to collect solutions that span distinct approaches; during training, GRPO is combined with a replay loss on this archive. The result is a post-trained model that improves accuracy while preserving more of the base model's solution diversity. On multiple text-to-SQL tasks, EliteReplay achieves a higher pass@128 than all baselines, producing up to 77% more distinct correct strategies than the strongest baselines. It preserves most of the base model's correct strategies, outperforming existing methods in strategy retention. This diversity translates into practical benefits on ambiguous questions, where EliteReplay covers both interpretations nearly twice as often as the strongest baseline on AmbiQT.

items.title: emem: A Content-Addressed, Verifiable Earth-Memory Protocol for AI Agents over Foundation-Model Embeddings - Poster
items.abstract: AI agents can change information when they exchange messages or complete long tasks. A value can be rounded. A location can change. An agent can use an observation from the wrong date. These errors can change decisions about the physical world. emem is an external memory protocol for AI agents. It uses content-addressed evidence records instead of paraphrases. An encoder creates a record from source information. An emem token identifies that record. A compatible receiving agent can resolve the token, decode the record, and check its contents. These operations do not depend on the AI model that sent the reference. Method This poster extends our earlier research on the emem protocol. We use a Sentinel-2A Level-2A observation from Keylong, India, dated 25 September 2026. The selected pixel has a normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) of 0.4709. We compare four handoff methods: prose, JSON, an opaque identifier, and a checked emem reference. We introduce controlled errors in values, spatial identity, time, source information, derivation, and record integrity. A deterministic receiver checks the record through these steps: Resolve the reference. Recompute the content hash. Check the observation identity. Verify the signature and log. Recompute the measurement when possible. Read the original source data independently when required. Results The deterministic receiver acted on corrupted evidence in 15 of 15 prose handoffs. With the complete emem verification sequence, it acted on none of 16 tested corruptions. We also found an error in emem's earlier satellite pixel reader. In 162 of 200 sampled records, the old reader selected a neighbouring pixel. We corrected the reader on 28 September 2026. None of 54 sampled records after the correction showed this error. The affected records had valid signatures. Thus, a valid signature established record integrity but did not establish measurement correctness. We also checked 780 records. All 780 passed the record-integrity and identity checks. Of these, 266 were recomputed bit for bit. Additional tests examine historical evidence, forest-screening inputs, foundation-model embeddings, and client interoperability. Verification limits A content address identifies exact record bytes. It does not establish physical truth. The records name their source files but do not include cryptographic hashes of those files. The current implementation also depends on keys managed by one operator. The protocol cannot independently establish the sensor's accuracy, the entity intended by the user, or the correctness of a final decision. An AI model can also fail if it removes a reference or ignores a verification refusal. These limits are part of the reported results. Contribution This work separates evidence integrity from measurement accuracy and decision correctness. It shows how AI agents can exchange exact evidence references across different systems. Each receiver can apply checks appropriate to its task. The protocol can also identify foundation-model embeddings as records. emem does not require a specific foundation model or encoder to remain in service. The demonstrated observations in this study come from existing Earth observation archives. Encoding directly at a capture device is a future application, not a result claimed in this poster. Research context Prepared for Agentic AI for Earth Observation, ESA Φ-lab and BIFOLD, Berlin, 19 October 2026. This poster is a companion to the original emem research paper. items.title: Emergence and development of observation practices in AI-assisted plant adaptation learning
items.abstract: Observation is a fundamental scientific practice in science learning, particularly for understanding gradual biological phenomena such as plant adaptation. Despite the increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in education, limited research has examined how AI-supported tools influence students' observation practices during authentic scientific inquiry. This study investigates the emergence and development of students' observation practices during plant adaptation learning supported by an AI-based identifier. A six-week mixed-methods exploratory study was conducted with 84 middle school students. Learning activities were organised into four phases: orientation, initial observation, AI-assisted identification, and re-observation and validation. Data were collected through observation sheets, students' observation notes, reflective journals, group discussions, and records of AI use. Quantitative analysis revealed significant differences in observation orientations across learning phases (Friedman test, p < .001), indicating changes in observation practices over time. Qualitative findings showed that students initially relied on AI-generated cues to guide their observations. Over time, however, observation practices shifted toward direct empirical observation and peer-supported validation through repeated comparisons of plant characteristics across environmental conditions. The findings reveal a developmental trajectory from AI-reliant observation to direct observation and collaborative validation, accompanied by a gradual reduction in dependence on AI-generated outputs. These findings suggest that AI may function as an initial observational scaffold, while more sophisticated observation practices emerge through repeated engagement with phenomena and collaborative reasoning.

items.title: Emergent Discrimination and Polarization in Multi-Agent Systems
items.abstract: We study theoretically how discrimination and polarization can emerge in a population of learning agents. Each agent uses an adaptive linear decision layer to map a language-model embedding of an issue to a binary opinion and maintains an evolving estimate of how much it trusts every other agent. Through pairwise interactions, agents update both their decision weights and trust estimates using an online Bayesian rule derived from teacher-student learning over a noisy channel. In-context-learning experiments with large language models qualitatively reproduce the predicted opinion and trust updates. We then assign each agent one of two arbitrary group labels, A or B, and model group bias by allowing a fraction $f_b$ of agents to shift its perceived agreement with each message by a strength $b$, a bias steering prejudice, depending on whether the sender and receiver share a label. We use order parameters from statistical mechanics to connect these local dynamics to collective states and transitions. Starting from uniformly random initial conditions, simulations reveal a rich phase diagram in the $(b,f_b)$ plane, comprising four collective states: spin-glass frustrated out-group favoritism, nondiscriminatory polarization, discrimination with opinion alignment, and discrimination without opinion alignment. Which state emerges depends on both the strength and prevalence of the bias. These results show how simple local learning dynamics can generate qualitatively distinct forms of polarization and discrimination, underscoring the need for population-level safety analysis of multi-agent systems. They also suggest measurable order parameters for characterizing analogous collective states in human societies.

items.title: Emerging Technologies in Teacher Professional Development Through the Lens of Self-Determination Theory: A Systematic Review
items.abstract: Purpose This systematic review analyzed 46 peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2025, revealing eight digital technology types, including Information and Communication Technology, Big Data, Artificial Intelligence, ChatGPT, Open Educational Resources, Massive Open Online Courses, Learning Management System, and Augmented Reality/Virtual Reality. Design/Approach/Method Technologies are organized across three conceptual layers: Infrastructure, Algorithm, and Application Layer. This study aims to investigate: (a) the key functions and implementation barriers of eight emerging technology types; (b) their impacts on teachers’ autonomy, competence, and relatedness; and (c) their impacts on the equity, quality, and efficiency of scalable teacher professional development. Findings Findings reveal that all technologies demonstrate dual impacts on the three psychological needs, both enabling and constraining, with competence most consistently supported across layers. Equity outcomes prove most challenging. Originality/Value This review concludes that effective technology integration requires human-centered ecosystems that amplify, not replace, teacher agency, advancing a value-rational approach recognizing teachers’ professional flourishing as an intrinsic good rather than an instrumental means.

items.title: Emotional intelligence and leadership development: past patterns, present realities and future directions in learning-oriented research
items.abstract: Purpose This study systematically examines the intersection of emotional intelligence (EI), leadership and learning-oriented development to understand how the field has evolved and its implications for human resource development (HRD) theory and practice. Design/methodology/approach A bibliometric analysis of 72 Scopus-indexed, ABDC-ranked journal articles published between 2015 and 2025 was conducted using Bibliometrix and VOSviewer. The analysis examined publication trends, collaboration networks, keyword co-occurrence patterns and thematic evolution within the field. Findings Seven thematic clusters emerged, with EI functioning as a central construct linking leadership, workplace learning and organizational outcomes. The findings indicate a shift from viewing EI as a fixed trait to conceptualizing it as a developable capability shaped through learning, reflection and relational experiences. The field has evolved from early conceptual exploration (2015–2018) to more empirical and context-driven research, particularly in the postpandemic period (2022–2025). While transformational leadership and EI remain dominant themes, adaptive, digital and crisis leadership have emerged as important areas of inquiry. The analysis also reveals a geographically diverse research landscape, although international collaboration remains uneven across regions. Originality/value This study provides a comprehensive bibliometric overview of the intersection between EI, leadership and learning and advances a learning-oriented perspective by positioning EI as a key capability within leadership development frameworks. By integrating leadership, workplace learning and organizational context, the study contributes to HRD and leadership scholarship and offers a structured foundation for future research and practice.

items.title: Employee engagement in SMEs: a bibliometric review and research agenda (1989–2024)
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the trends, intellectual structure, frequently explored topics, and future research directions in employee engagement within small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), thereby providing insights for theoretical development and HRM practice. Design/methodology/approach This review applied bibliometric methods to examine 730 documents indexed in the Scopus database and published between 1989 and 2024. The study utilized descriptive analyses and science mapping techniques, including co-citation and keyword co-occurrence analyses. Findings The findings reveal growing academic interest, highlighting a shift from transactional to transformational human resource management. Further research in South America and Africa is needed to improve the generalizability of the existing knowledge base. Three main clusters were identified along with influential authors and key theories in each area: “Integrated Psychological and Occupational Health”, “Dynamic Organizational Studies”, and “Work Engagement and Burnout”. Temporal co-word analysis shows the enduring relevance of job satisfaction and organizational commitment, with an emerging focus on the impacts of COVID-19 and sustainability, including corporate social responsibility (CSR), reflecting a trend toward integrating sustainable practices into business strategies. Originality/value To the authors' knowledge, this is the first bibliometric review focused specifically on employee engagement in the SME context, an important HRM issue for the effective management of human resources.

items.title: Empowerment as an innovative trend in the Occupational Health and Safety Management System (SG-SST).
items.abstract: El presente trabajo muestra las tendencias administrativas contemporáneas como estrategias innovadoras aplicadas a las organizaciones, especialmente, el Empowerment que ayuda a reforzar el liderazgo y a incentivar la participación activa de los colaboradores en el sistema de gestión del riesgo la seguridad y salud en el trabajo (SG-SST). A partir de la revisión de la norma internacional ISO 45001 de 2018 y el Decreto 1072 de 2015 se logra evidenciar una problemática relacionada en la baja participación del capital humano en el tema de la prevención y la identificación de riesgos laborales. En este sentido, esta tendencia se propone como solución y estrategia para potencializar la participación activa de los colaboradores, incentivar la cultura del autocuidado en todas las áreas de la compañía. Lo cual contribuye a tener líderes íntegros, proporciona acciones preventivas más efectivas y eleva la comunicación interna. Por lo tanto, se verifica avances en el SG-SST enfocado en el liderazgo, en la asignación de responsabilidades, en la motivación de la participación activa de los colaboradores y la utilización de los diferentes recursos, integrando esta tendencia administrativa que permite mejorar de manera continua todo el proceso organizacional haciendo compañías más productivas, fortaleciendo la cultura de prevención de riesgos, accidentes e incidentes laborales.

items.title: Engagement in AI-Mediated Informal Digital Learning of English: An Adaptive Intelligence Perspective on Motivational, Psychological, and Technological Resources
items.abstract: Using adaptive intelligence as a theoretical lens, the study investigates how L2 motivational selves are associated with AI-IDLE engagement through psychological capital (PsyCap) and L2 grit and whether these indirect associations vary with AI literacy among 1025 Chinese university EFL learners. The proposed model was tested using structural equation modeling (SEM). For the ideal L2 self, associations with engagement emerged both directly and indirectly through PsyCap and L2 grit, whereas the ought-to L2 self showed an indirect association through PsyCap and no direct association with engagement. Higher AI literacy corresponded to stronger associations of both PsyCap and L2 grit with engagement. The two motivational self-guides were therefore associated with engagement through different psychological pathways, with AI literacy related to variation in the strength of these pathways. From an adaptive intelligence perspective, this conditional pattern indicates that the relevance of PsyCap and L2 grit to AI-IDLE engagement varies with learners’ AI literacy. These findings extend the application of adaptive intelligence to informal human–AI learning.

items.title: ENHANCING INTELLIGIBILITY AND LEARNER AUTONOMY IN EFL PRONUNCIATION INSTRUCTION THROUGH AI-DRIVEN PEDAGOGICAL FEEDBACK
items.abstract: Modern English as a Foreign Language (EFL) pronunciation instruction has shifted its primary goal from native-like accent imitation to functional intelligibility and comprehensibility. Despite this paradigm shift, traditional classroom settings often struggle to provide personalized, real-time diagnostic feedback due to large class sizes and time constraints. This study investigates the pedagogical integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven speech analysis and automated acoustic feedback in EFL pronunciation teaching. Synthesizing contemporary literature on Computer-Assisted Pronunciation Training (CAPT) and feedback literacy, this paper examines how AI feedback impacts learner autonomy, segmental clarity, and suprasegmental awareness. The review reveals that AI tools provide consistent, low-anxiety practice environments that facilitate cognitive noticing and self-correction. However, over-reliance on automated metrics without explicit pedagogical framing can result in mechanical practice detached from communicative contexts. To reconcile these dynamics, this article introduces a conceptual Scaffolded Pedagogical Feedback Model (SPFM) that integrates AI-generated acoustic diagnostic data, structured peer dialogue, and teacher-mediated instructional intervention. The framework highlights the necessity of developing student feedback literacy to transform automated output into actionable learning strategies. Keywords: EFL pronunciation instruction, Computer-Assisted Pronunciation Training (CAPT), artificial intelligence, intelligibility, learner autonomy, feedback literacy.

items.title: Enhancing Students’ Understanding of Anthropometry-Based Classroom Chair Design in Senior High Schools and Vocational High Schools
items.abstract: This community service activity aimed to improve the understanding of senior high school and vocational high school students regarding classroom chair design based on anthropometric principles. The activity was conducted face-to-face at partner schools in Jakarta through ergonomics lectures, demonstrations of seated anthropometric measurements, percentile calculation exercises, and discussions on applying measurement results to chair dimensions. The anthropometric dimensions introduced included popliteal height, buttock-popliteal length, hip breadth, sitting shoulder height, and sitting elbow height. Evaluation was conducted through pre-tests and post-tests, question-and-answer sessions, observation of practical activities, analysis, and reflection. The results showed an improvement in participants’ understanding of anthropometric dimensions relevant to chair design. The proportion of participants who provided fully correct answers increased from 42.0% in the pre-test to 83.3% in the post-test. Participants were also able to identify the relationship between body dimensions and chair components, explain the risks associated with dimensional mismatch, and formulate initial principles for determining seat height, seat depth, seat width, and backrest dimensions. The activity demonstrated that contextual, practice-based learning can enhance students’ ergonomic literacy and encourage data-based thinking in evaluating learning facilities.

items.title: Enhancing Writer Identity Through Generative AI
items.abstract: The rapid integration of generative AI tools has transformed writing instruction, raising questions about authorship, agency, and academic integrity in teacher education. Unlike search engines, generative AI produces synthesized text that supports brainstorming, drafting, revising, and feedback. While these tools can reduce cognitive load and enhance higher-order thinking, they may also weaken productive struggle, writer identity, and promote overreliance without intentional instructional design. These issues are especially relevant for preservice teachers who must learn to use AI both ethically and instructionally. Grounded in self-regulation, self-efficacy, metacognitive theory, and the cognitive process model of writing, this study frames AI as metacognitive scaffolding for writing development. The framework highlights a gap between preservice teachers' frequent use of AI and their limited readiness to teach with it. The article argues that intentional, theory-driven integration can support planning, monitoring, and reflection while preserving student voice and autonomy. I

items.title: EnjoyEAT: Embodied Interaction for Behavior-Aware, CBT-Informed Eating-Disorder Support
items.abstract: Digital tools for eating-disorder support often rely on retrospective self-report or text-based prompts, offering limited support for the embodied, temporally unfolding nature of eating episodes. We introduce Embodied Therapeutic Interaction (ETI), a design framework for translating CBT-informed principles into phase-aligned, behavior-aware interactions, and instantiate it in EnjoyEAT, a prototype combining surface electromyography sensing with pre-meal preparation, in-meal awareness cues, and post-meal reflection. Formative inquiry with experts and people with lived experience yielded requirements concerning temporal vulnerability, bodily awareness, emotional safety, and autonomy-preserving feedback. A four-week, uncontrolled in-the-wild study with 12 participants reporting subclinical tendencies showed decreased EDE-Q scores and positive user-experience ratings. Interviews indicated feedback helped some participants notice and reflect on eating patterns, while revealing tensions around sensing accuracy, setup burden, and sustained engagement. Though not a clinical intervention, EnjoyEAT offers HCI design evidence about phase alignment, soft embodiment, reflective mediation, and emotionally careful feedback for situated recovery support.

items.title: Epistemic Hidden Defects in Artificial Intelligence: Classical ʿIlal al-Ḥadīth as a Framework for AI Verification
items.abstract: This working paper examines whether the classical methodology of ʿilal al-Ḥadīth—the detection of hidden defects in apparently sound reports—can provide a useful conceptual framework for evaluating artificial-intelligence outputs in specialist knowledge environments. It develops the concept of the “epistemic hidden defect”: a weakness in provenance, attribution, inference, context, evidential hierarchy, or scholarly status that may remain concealed beneath a fluent and apparently authoritative AI-generated response. Drawing on classical Hadith-critical methodology and contemporary AI research, the paper distinguishes computational capability from scholarly authority. It develops the concepts of the Authority Ceiling, Digital Isnād, competence-specific human oversight, and the No-Autonomous-Grading Principle as safeguards for AI-assisted scholarship. The paper argues for an AI-assisted rather than AI-autonomous model of specialist research, in which computational systems widen the evidential field while consequential scholarly judgement remains traceable, reviewable, and accountable.

items.title: Epistemological Collapse
items.abstract: This chapter examines how generative AI disrupts the epistemic foundations of take-home academic assignments. It argues that written products can no longer be reliably interpreted as evidence of student thinking, as AI enables the production of fluent, academically credible work without corresponding cognitive effort. Drawing on teaching practice, the chapter shows how student submissions have shifted in form, tone, and ownership. It then reframes the problem as one of construct validity, where the link between performance and learning becomes unstable. In response, the chapter proposes presence-based assessment as a partial solution and argues that meaningful change requires institutional redesign of assessment architecture.

items.title: ESL ASSESSMENT IN THE AGE OF AI: SERBIAN ESL TEACHERS’ ATTITUDES TOWARDS THE USE OF CHATGPT
items.abstract: Following the introduction of publicly accessible AI and LLMs, they have gradually started to be adopted in the ESL classroom. Recent studies have revealed that these tools have had a wider impact on ESL assessment, allowing for enhanced accuracy, efficiency, and person alization in language evaluation. However, how widely these technologies are understood and used by teachers is still being investigated. This study explores how Serbian ESL teachers use and perceive ChatGPT as a tool for assessing student work. The study employs a mixed-methods approach, combining survey data from 53 participants with follow-up interviews from 10 educa tors to examine their tendencies, habits, and opinions regarding ChatGPT for assessment. Find ings revealed that grammar and vocabulary are the language skills which Serbian ESL teachers assessed most often using ChatGPT, while skills such as speaking, listening, and critical thinking were rarely assessed using AI. Teachers also expressed moderate trust in the tool’s ability to detect grammar and syntax errors, but were concerned about its limitations. These limitations included ChatGPT’s ability to provide accurate assessment, its tendency to give vague feedback, and its lack of contextual understanding. While many teachers recognized its ability to save time for as sessment tasks, they also recognized their own limited experiences with AI tools and stressed the need for human oversight, formal training, and ethical safeguards. This study indicated that even though ChatGPT does not yet have widespread use in the Serbian ESL classroom, interviewees frequently emphasized that it should be used as a supplementary tool to assist teachers, but that guidelines and professional training on its use need to be provided to the teachers before they would readily implement it in the classroom.

items.title: Estimating the threat of AI-agent responding across online survey platforms
items.abstract: Recent research and advances in LLMs have led to widespread concern that AI agents could pose as human online survey-takers. However, it remains unclear how prevalent AI agents are on survey research platforms and how to effectively detect AI agents. We validated a series of AI detection tests that effectively separated verified-human participants from both prompted commercial and purpose-built AI agents. Using these tests, we collected surveys on seven online platforms and find wide variation in rates of respondents failing AI tests, ranging from 6 to 41% across platforms (compared to a 2.4% false-positive rate for in-person human participants). We further demonstrate that undetected AI agents can impact the results of online surveys. Our findings suggest that while there is an urgent need for AI detection tests and consistent, systematic monitoring of data quality on online platforms, some platforms currently appear to provide data with a low rate of AI agents.

items.title: Ethical AI Governance in Marketing
items.abstract: The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into marketing activities has transformed the way organizations interact with customers, analyze consumer behavior, and deliver personalized services. Despite the significant opportunities provided by AI technologies, their widespread adoption has also raised critical concerns regarding ethical risks, data privacy, algorithmic bias, transparency, and customer trust. This chapter explores the role of responsible AI practices in mitigating marketing-related risks and enhancing customer confidence in AI-driven marketing environments. The chapter adopts a conceptual and analytical approach to examine the principles of ethical AI governance in marketing organizations, focusing on transparency, accountability, fairness, privacy protection, and human oversight. It further discusses how responsible AI practices contribute to reducing reputational risks, improving organizational credibility, and strengthening long-term customer relationships.

items.title: Ethical Integration of Artificial Intelligence in Education Through Human Agency, Equity, and Sustainable Innovation
items.abstract: This chapter examines the ethical integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in education, emphasizing the need to align technological advancement with human agency, equity and sustainable innovation. It explores how AI is reshaping instructional practices, assessment systems, and educational governance across global and African contexts. Drawing on framework s such as UNESCO's recommendations on AI ethics and the OECD principles, this chapter per the authors analyses critical issues including algorithmic bias, overdependence, and the erosion of creativity. It further highlights the central role of teachers as ethical stewards, mediators, and facilitators of responsible AI use. The discussion underscores the importance of inclusive and assistive AI technologies in expanding access for marginalised learners while cautioning against reinforcing existing inequalities. Additionally, the chapter addresses policy, governance and accountability mechanisms necessary for ethical AI development advocating a human-centered approach that ensures AI supports educational goals.

items.title: Evaluating an LLM Pipeline for End-to-End MCDA
items.abstract: Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) requires human involvement at every stage of its process. This paper proposes a systematic LLM evaluation protocol for end-to-end MCDA pipelines, using published expert rankings as a benchmark. In addition, it implements a four-stage LLM pipeline as a case study applying the protocol to three leading LLMs across five benchmark problems selected to vary in application domain and in the number of alternatives. The protocol comprises 225 independent pipeline executions (3 models × 5 repetitions × 3 temperatures × 5 problems); each execution applies three MCDA methods (LLM-weighted linear scoring, TOPSIS, PROMETHEE II) to the same LLM-generated score matrix, yielding 675 method-specific outputs in total. Consistent with a smaller pilot study of this protocol, differences between models are small relative to problem identity (Kruskal–Wallis, H = 1.10, p = 0.577, η2 = 0.005; a small but significant effect emerges once problem identity is controlled for, η2 = 0.6%), while problem identity remains the dominant performance factor—and a larger one than previously observed (η2 = 0.761, H = 170.51, p < 0.001, N = 225 executions). Kendall’s τ ranges from −0.34 on a ten-alternative problem to 0.56 on a four-alternative problem; a permutation test against random rankings indicates that two of the five benchmark problems produced agreement below chance level, while two problems produced agreement above chance level; since the test treats executions as independent, these deviations should be read as descriptive rather than inferential. Top-3 Accuracy ranges from 10.1% to 72.1% across problems, relative to chance baselines of 30% to 75%. Reliability varies strongly across problems, and the compensatory/non-compensatory distinction from the pilot does not fully explain this. In this pipeline, the scoring stage receives the names of the alternatives and criteria but not the numerical decision data, so the results reflect the LLM’s prior knowledge; its role as an explanatory factor is proposed as a hypothesis for future testing.

items.title: Evaluating and Improving Static Application Security Testing Tools for Rust
items.abstract: Rust has become a popular systems programming language in recent years because of its strong guarantees on memory and concurrency safety. Many types of system software have been re-implemented in Rust. However, Rust programs can still suffer from common memory and concurrency vulnerabilities due to unsafe code and misunderstandings of its complex mechanisms. To mitigate such vulnerabilities, developers often rely on static application security testing (SAST) tools. However, the effectiveness of existing Rust SAST tools on real-world vulnerabilities remains underexplored. In this paper, we first conduct an empirical evaluation of mainstream Rust SAST tools using security vulnerabilities identified in real-world Rust applications. We systematically assess their effectiveness, uncover common weaknesses, and analyze the root causes behind them. Motivated by the study, we propose TRUST, a large language model (LLM)-assisted automated testing framework. TRUST automatically analyzes the official Rust reference to derive and implement semantics-preserving transformations. It leverages these transformations to generate mutant programs for evaluating Rust SAST tools and uncovering potential faults within them. Overall, TRUST has revealed 46 faults across six popular SAST tools, 17 of which have been confirmed. In addition, our study yields ten empirical findings and four practical lessons that provide actionable guidance for developing more effective, robust, and maintainable Rust SAST tools.

items.title: Evaluating Inquiry Learning in LLM-Based Agents: Hypothesizing, Reasoning, and Exploration
items.abstract: Scientific inquiry involves iterative cycles of exploration, hypothesis generation, and reasoning over observations to uncover relationships in complex systems. Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in several components of this process, including inductive reasoning, hypothesis generation, and data analysis. However, prior work typically evaluates these abilities in isolation, leaving open how models integrate them across a full inquiry cycle. In this work, we introduce a framework for evaluating LLMs' inquiry capabilities in a unified, interactive setting. We extend the Countdown task to a mathematical environment where an agent probes the system by manipulating variables, collecting observations, and inferring relationships between them. This setup enables analysis of exploration strategies, causal discovery, and hypothesis refinement during inquiry. Across seven LLMs and multiple prompting strategies, our experiments reveal limited inherent inquiry capabilities and low success rates in discovering the underlying expressions. However, structured guidance inspired by educational scaffolding significantly improves performance. Our findings highlight current limitations of LLMs in strategic exploration and iterative hypothesis refinement, and show how simple guidance strategies developed for human learners in inquiry learning can support more effective inquiry behavior.

items.title: Evaluating Large Language Model–Derived Outputs as Psychological Measures: A Five-Domain Psychometric Framework With Application to Daily Stress
items.abstract: Abstract Background Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to quantify psychological constructs from natural language, yet their outputs are typically evaluated only as predictions of an external label. When that label is itself imperfect, optimizing prediction conflates label agreement with construct measurement. No study has applied a multidomain measurement-oriented evaluation to LLM-derived psychological outputs. Objective We applied 5 psychometric evaluation domains to LLM-derived outputs to test whether measurement-oriented evaluation surfaces properties that prediction-oriented evaluation does not: extraction repeatability, convergent validity with a lexicon-based tool, ecological concurrent validity decomposed into within-person and between-person components, incremental value in a 4-arm comparison with that tool, and method-blinded expert evaluation with structured error attribution. Methods Thirteen linguistic features were extracted by GPT-5.2 (OpenAI) from 3556 person-days of daily voice narratives collected from 279 call center workers over 15 days via ecological momentary assessment. Features were evaluated across the 5 domains, with Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count, version 22, as the lexicon-based comparator. Multimodel robustness was assessed by re-extracting all features with Google Gemini 2.5 Flash. Results Features showed high repeatability (mean intraclass correlation coefficient=0.987), construct-dependent convergent validity (Spearman ρ=0.08 to 0.79), and within-person tracking of same-day stress (negative emotion β=0.68). In a 4-arm comparison (baseline, baseline plus lexicon features, baseline plus LLM-derived features, and baseline plus both), LLM features increased explained variance in daily stress from 13.2% to 30.4%, versus 16.9% for the lexicon-based comparator. Among transcripts sampled for maximal method discordance, experts preferred LLM-derived profiles in 83.7% (261/312) of blinded decisions. Error analysis showed that 53% (35/66) of false-positive attributions reflected reference-label limitations, not model failures. Re-extraction with Google Gemini 2.5 Flash replicated key properties (person-level r =0.94). Three phenomena were visible under measurement-oriented evaluation that prediction-oriented evaluation does not typically examine: divergence between within-person and between-person effects, reference-label limitations as a dominant error source, and moderation of feature meaning by individual differences. Conclusions Prediction metrics alone are insufficient for evaluating LLM-derived psychological measures. Measurement-oriented evaluation revealed properties, including level-dependent effects and asymmetric error attribution, that have direct implications for how LLM-based assessment studies interpret their results. For clinical use, the measure is a complement to existing screening instruments for longitudinal monitoring, not a stand-alone diagnostic.

items.abstract: This study evaluated intrinsic and extrinsic motivation determinants affecting faculty job performance and retention at Asian Institute of Computer Studies (AICS) Commonwealth, Quezon City (N=35). Using descriptive-correlational design, findings revealed very high intrinsic motivation (M=4.51 fulfillment, M=4.40 autonomy) but low extrinsic salary satisfaction (M=2.68). Regional salary disparities were identified as major push factor (M=4.11) prompting migration to public institutions, with uncertain 3-5 year retention (M=3.06). Five policy interventions are proposed: compensation restructuring, workload optimization, non-monetary pathways, facilities upgrade, and participative leadership.

items.title: Evaluation Awareness Beyond English: Do LLMs Act Differently When Tested in Indic Languages?
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can often tell when they are being tested. This ability, known as evaluation awareness, can lead models to act more cautiously during safety evaluations than in real use. Existing work has studied evaluation awareness almost entirely in English, although models serve users in many languages. Indic languages are spoken by over a billion people, yet evaluation awareness remains almost entirely unstudied in them. We test four instruction-tuned models from three families in five Indic languages alongside English. A set of cues varies whether the model is told that it is monitored and whether the monitoring is a safety test. Models refuse harmful requests more often when they are told that they are being tested. This increase appears in all four models and all six languages. In Indic languages, refusal of harmful requests rises by 14.4 percentage points on average. The test cue also brings Indic refusal of harmful requests level with English, but raises refusal of benign Indic requests from 6.9% to 11.3%. We release all 47,880 judged responses to support further work. These results suggest that safety evaluations in Indic languages may not reflect how models treat their everyday users.

items.title: Evaluation of ChatGPT for Myocardial Infarction Health Information: Expert Accuracy Assessment and User Trust Survey
items.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence chatbots, particularly ChatGPT, have emerged as increasingly popular sources of health information for the general public. However, concerns persist regarding the accuracy, safety, and appropriateness of AI-generated medical advice, especially for life-threatening conditions such as myocardial infarction. Objectives: This study aimed to evaluate the accuracy, completeness, and safety of ChatGPT-generated responses and information to public questions about heart attacks, assess user perceptions and trust, and compare AI-generated content with expert-validated sources. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted between January and March 2026. A total of 73 commonly asked heart attack-related questions were submitted to ChatGPT (GPT-4), and responses were independently evaluated by two expert reviewers and one external reviewer using standardized rubric assessing accuracy, completeness, clarity, safety, and tone. Inter-rater reliability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients. In parallel, a survey of 352 participants evaluated user perceptions, trust, and behavioral use of ChatGPT for medical information. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, group comparisons, correlation analyses, and multivariable regression models to identify predictors of trust and satisfaction. Results: Expert reviewers assigned high ratings for accuracy (mean: 4.62 ± 0.62 and 4.48 ± 0.63) and safety (mean: 4.78 ± 0.51 and 4.05 ± 0.50), with substantial inter-rater agreement (ICC = 0.788). In contrast, the external reviewer documented considerably lower completeness ratings (2.59 ± 0.57), revealing deficiencies in information coverage. Remarkably, 40.6% of respondents indicated they had followed ChatGPT's medical recommendations without seeking professional consultation, while 17.6% reported depending on the chatbot during urgent medical situations. Levels of user trust and satisfaction were moderate, showing significant correlations with perceived accuracy, usage frequency, and healthcare-related educational background. Conclusions: Expert assessments confirmed that ChatGPT generally provides accurate and safe cardiovascular health information; nevertheless, considerable inter-reviewer variability—especially the markedly lower completeness scores from the external evaluator—reveals significant gaps in content depth. These results indicate that ChatGPT functions more appropriately as an adjunctive educational resource rather than a replacement for professional medical consultation, emphasizing the necessity for enhanced safety mechanisms, clearer user instructions, and standardized content protocols when addressing high-stakes health topics. ChatGPT should be considered an adjunctive resource rather than a substitute for urgent professional medical assessment in suspected heart attack cases.

items.title: Evolution of Computational Chemistry Applied to Virtual Drug Screening: A Mini-Review
items.abstract: Computational chemistry has become a strategic component of drug design by enabling the evaluation of large chemical libraries, the investigation of molecular interactions, and the prioritization of candidates before experimental testing. This mini-review examines the evolution of computational chemistry applied to virtual screening, highlighting its main approaches, the physicochemical filters used for compound selection, and the incorporation of artificial intelligence-based methods. A narrative review of the literature was conducted using Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, SciELO, and ScienceDirect, supplemented by Google Scholar. Publications from 2015 to 2026 were prioritized, along with seminal studies on the Lipinski, Ghose, Egan, Muegge, and Veber filters. The literature indicates that structure-based and ligand-based drug design provide complementary strategies for the identification and optimization of bioactive molecules. Methods such as molecular docking, molecular dynamics, QSAR, pharmacophore modeling, and ADMET prediction improve selection efficiency, whereas descriptors such as molecular weight, lipophilicity, solubility, polar surface area, ionization, flexibility, and the fraction of sp³ carbons (Fsp³) aid in assessing pharmacokinetic potential. Machine learning and deep learning have expanded the ability to explore vast chemical spaces and predict molecular properties. However, the reliability of computational results depends on the quality of the structures, data, and models employed. In conclusion, integrating computational tools, physicochemical criteria, and experimental validation can reduce costs, support decision-making, and increase the efficiency of therapeutic candidate discovery.

items.title: Examining K-2 Educators' Perceptions of Project Read AI in Developing Instructional Materials
items.abstract: This qualitative study examined K-2 early childhood educators' perceptions of Project Read AI, an artificial intelligence platform designed specifically to support phonics-based instruction aligned with the Science of Reading. Grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model, the study investigated both the perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness of the platform among six kindergarten through second-grade teachers at a suburban New York elementary school. Findings indicated that educators perceived the platform as generally user-friendly and expressed strong intentions to integrate it into their practice. Evaluations of instructional materials yielded mixed results: the Decodable Game was viewed as a highly effective engagement tool, the Lola Science of Reading chatbot produced lesson frameworks valued as supplemental resources, and the Decodable Text Generator showed instructional promise but required improvements. Implications are given for educator practice, professional development, and future research on AI-powered literacy tools in early childhood education.

items.title: Expanded Urban Innovation for the Twenty-Second Century: From Cutting Emissions to Enabling Flourishing Lives on a Thriving Planet
items.abstract: Cities are central to the climate challenge, but much research on urban climate action still focuses on emissions reductions within existing systems. This literature review assesses existing research and literature, including work on human-need-driven innovation for global sustainability and the export of globally sustainable solutions. Rather than limiting urban climate action to measures aimed at reaching zero emissions, the review examines an expanded urban innovation agenda in which cities are studied as incubators and exporters of innovations that support flourishing lives for all on a flourishing planet. The review synthesizes insights from sustainability transitions, sociotechnical systems, well-being economics, artificial intelligence, and brain science. Case studies from different cities illustrate how some urban innovation agendas are already shifting. The comparison highlights how a focus on flourishing lives can mobilize start-ups, youth, and public institutions, while addressing equity and positioning cities as actors in the next generation of urban climate action.

items.title: Experimental evaluation of the effect of the feed bowl design on the eating behavior of domestic cats in the context of whisker stress
items.abstract: Aim of the study. To evaluate the effect of feed bowl design on the eating behavior of domestic cats with emphasis on the phenomenon of whisker stress. Materials and methods. A prospective within-subject study with sequential exposure to two feeding conditions was conducted in 26 clinically healthy domestic cats. Animals were sequentially fed from a standard deep narrow bowl (control) and a wide shallow bowl (experiment) with a 3-day adaptation period. The following parameters were recorded: amount of feed consumed, amount of dropped feed, number of approaches to the bowl, presence of pauses and attempts to extract feed with a paw. Statistical analysis was performed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, Fisher's exact test and binomial test. Results. No statistically significant differences in feed consumption were found between the two conditions (p > 0,05). When using the wide shallow bowl, no feed dropping was observed (0%), whereas when feeding from the standard bowl, dropping occurred in 38,5% of cats (p < 0,05). In the preference test, cats did not show a preference for either bowl (p > 0,05). Behavioral markers of sensory discomfort were not recorded. Conclusions. Bowl design affects feeding ergonomics and the amount of spilled feed but does not confirm the existence of whisker stress as a systemic phenomenon in domestic cats. Recommendations for the use of wide bowls may be justified by practical considerations of convenience.

items.title: Expert evaluation of ChatGPT-generated responses to patient questions in conventional and fast-track total knee arthroplasty
items.abstract: Fast-track total knee arthroplasty (TKA) asks patients to understand early mobilization, early discharge, opioid-sparing analgesia, and selective use of drains and catheters. We evaluated expert-rated quality of ChatGPT responses to patient questions about these pathway-specific concepts alongside conventional TKA questions. In this cross-sectional evaluation, three arthroplasty surgeons independently scored responses to 50 conventional TKA and 20 investigator-developed fast-track questions in four domains on 5-point scales. The conventional questions were selected by a multidisciplinary panel; the fast-track questions did not undergo the same selection process. Response-level means were compared descriptively and with exploratory Mann-Whitney U tests. Seventy responses received 210 expert assessments. Recalculated mean ± SD scores across individual ratings were 4.99 ± 0.15 for accuracy, 4.98 ± 0.14 for completeness, 4.98 ± 0.17 for safety, and 5.00 ± 0.07 for readability. Each of the 20 fast-track responses received a score of 5 from each of the three raters in all four domains (Supplementary Table S1). Nevertheless, question-set construction differed and scores clustered at the ceiling, so the exploratory comparison does not establish equivalence. Experts gave high ratings to the evaluated responses, including those on fast-track concepts. The observed data do not establish equivalence between question sets: the fast-track ratings require source-data verification, the sets were selected differently, and scores were concentrated at the maximum. Clinician review remains appropriate for protocol-dependent and safety-related advice. Not applicable.

items.title: Explainability Aware Heterogeneous Temporal Graph Transformer for Automated Genetic Disorder Detection from Genomic Data
items.abstract: Genetic disorders affect millions worldwide, posing major challenges for accurate diagnosis and effective treatments. New developments in genomic technologies, especially Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS), have enhanced the classification of genetic modification and improved diagnostic abilities. Moreover, the Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) methods emerged as efficient tools for evaluating the intricate genomic data and determining the patterns, which can be generally complex to identify by employing conventional analytical techniques. Additionally, the Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) has developed as a significant constituent in the analysis of genomic data by enhancing the interpretability of DL methods and showing the contribution of main genetic features involved in the detection of genetic disorders. This study presents an Explainability-Aware Heterogeneous Temporal Graph Transformer for Automated Genetic Disorder Detection (XHTGT-AGDD) approach. The primary objective of the proposed model is to improve the reliability and accuracy of genetic disorder detection from genomic data by integrating advanced techniques. Initially, preprocessing is performed using quantile transformation to normalize the input data for robust analysis. Following preprocessing, feature selection is performed using the fire hawk optimizer to identify the most informative feature subsets from the genomic data. Besides, the classification task is accomplished using a heterogeneous temporal graph transformer, which captures complex relationships and temporal dependencies among genomic features. To further refine the learning process, hippopotamus optimization algorithm is employed for model optimization. In addition, an explainability mechanism based on SHAP is incorporated to interpret the model predictions and highlight the individual genetic features toward the final decision. The experimental result analysis of the XHTGT-AGDD model is performed using a benchmark dataset. The simulation results reported the enhanced results of the XHTGT-AGDD technique in terms of several measures, achieving an accuracy of 99.12%. Therefore, the proposed model provides reliable and effective performance for automated genetic disorder detection from genomic data.

items.title: Explainable AI-Driven Intelligent Video Summarization for Next-Generation Video Production and Content Management
items.abstract: This chapter reviews the development of video summarisation using handcrafted features and deep learning models, the recent advances in transformer-based, vision-language, multimodal learning, and large language models for video summarisation. It introduces the main steps of the summarization pipeline: keyframes extraction, keyshots generation, importance score prediction and summary generation. Particular focus is given to explainability techniques like LIME, Grad-CAM, attention maps and multi-granular explanations, and how frame, shot, semantic, and story-level explanations can help to increase the transparency and user trust. Applications in film and media production, OTT platforms, news, education and surveillance are also discussed as well as challenges concerning explainability evaluation, computational complexity, privacy, ethics and scalability. The future involves explainable LLMs, personalized summarization, human in the loop AI, interactive systems and foundation models.

items.title: Explainable deep graph attention learning with enhanced residual SwinV2 transformer for interpretable facial paralysis severity assessment
items.abstract: Facial paralysis is a severely disabling disorder that causes weakness or damage to facial muscles, thus leading to abnormal or asymmetric facial movements. Timely and precise detection and grading of facial paralysis is more essential for appropriate treatments and rehabilitations. Conventionally, facial image analysis was a manual process relying on expert proficiency. Recently, deep learning (DL) techniques have revolutionized the field, especially in the context of facial and clinical image analyses. While DL enables automatic, accurate facial recognition, its black-box nature restricts its use in healthcare. Therefore, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) is integrated to enhance transparency that provides visual evidence for medical decision-making. This study introduces an Explainable Deep Graph Attention Learning Framework for Facial Paralysis Identification (XDGAL-FPI). The proposed model is designed to automatically identify the severity of facial paralysis using facial image data. Initially, the input images are preprocessed, including face detection and alignment, color space conversion and contrast enhancement, noise reduction, normalization, and data augmentation to improve the quality and consistency of the input data. Besides, deep feature representations are extracted using an Enhanced Residual SwinV2 Transformer. The extracted features are then provided to a Heterogeneous Graph Attention Network that models the relational dependencies between multiple facial regions, such as the eyes, eyebrows, and mouth, for precise severity classification. Additionally, to improve the training efficiency and convergence behavior of the model, the Ranger optimizer is employed. Furthermore, the GradCAM + + technique is integrated to improve model interpretability by highlighting the important facial regions that contribute to the model’s prediction. The effectiveness of the proposed model is assessed using YouTube Facial Paralysis (YFP) Updated Dataset, which contains 14, 389 images categorized into four severity levels across different facial regions. The experimental results indicate that the proposed XDGAL-FPI model achieves improved performance compared with existing approaches across various evaluation metrics. Thus, the proposed XDGAL-FPI model can serve as a reliable and interpretable tool for automated facial paralysis severity assessment. The source code of this study is available at https://github.com/researcher010-debug/XDGAL-FPI .

items.title: Explaining the Roles of Experts in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs for Personalization
items.abstract: Personalization of Large Language Models (LLMs) is increasingly important for user-centric applications, yet prior methods mainly adapt dense LLMs, whose polysemantic neurons, each encoding multiple unrelated concepts, hinder localizing the components behind personalization, and thus understanding and controlling it. We propose to personalize Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs, which sparsely route each token to a few specialized experts, reducing polysemanticity and enabling such localization. We adapt three open-weight MoE LLMs on a large-scale personalization dataset and train crosscoders on paired activations of the personalized and non-personalized models to learn interpretable personalized latents, from which we identify the experts encoding distinct personalization features. The personalized MoE LLMs perform competitively with dense LLMs while activating only a fraction of their parameters, exhibit lower polysemanticity than dense LLMs with similar active parameters, and, within the same model family, yield personalized latents that are less shared with the non-personalized model. Causal interventions show that these latents suffice to recover the personalized model's behavior and that boosting their associated experts moves the non-personalized model toward it, revealing distinct routing paths for different personalization features.

items.title: Exploring AI-resistant assessments: insights from Large Language Models creating and completing their own research assessments
items.abstract: Higher education institutions have been grappling with the impact of Large Language Models (LLMs) on teaching and learning. LLMs like ChatGPT, Claude, and DeepSeek, can produce high-quality text with a single prompt. This is particularly concerning in research modules, where students are expected to showcase their work in a text-based format. In this study, ChatGPT, Claude, and DeepSeek were prompted to develop three research assessments that an LLM should not be able to complete and were subsequently prompted with the instructions generated. The purpose was to explore the influence of assessment instructions and characteristics on the ability of these models to generate complete responses. The instructions and characteristics included written text, oral discussions, physical attendance, contextual access, realistic content, lecturer approval, and the inclusion of multiple components. The most influential characteristic was the inclusion of an oral component. Other noteworthy characteristics were requiring students to attend live events and including multiple staged components. These findings contribute to the ongoing exploration of assessment design in the age of AI and LLMs.

items.title: Exploring Empowerment Challenges Facing SMMEs in the Nelson Mandela Bay Automotive Industry
items.abstract: Small, Medium and Micro Enterprises (SMMEs) play a critical role in South Africa's automotive industry by promoting economic growth, supplier development, and employment creation. However, persistent empowerment challenges continue to constrain their participation in automotive value chains and limit their contribution to youth skills development and workforce development pathways. This study aimed to explore the empowerment challenges facing SMMEs within the Nelson Mandela Bay automotive industry and to examine how these challenges influence opportunities for youth skills formation and sustainable workforce development. A qualitative case study design was adopted, employing purposive and snowball sampling to recruit 15 participants comprising SMME owners, Sector Development representatives, and Automotive Industry Development Centre (AIDC) officials. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analysed using six-phase thematic analysis. The findings identified six interrelated themes that constrain SMME empowerment: access and resources, skills and training, communication and information, policy and leadership, infrastructure and operations, and motivation and organisational culture. Collectively, these barriers restrict SMMEs' competitiveness, reduce their ability to participate in supplier development initiatives, and weaken their capacity to provide workplace learning opportunities, apprenticeships, and technical skills development for young people entering the automotive industry. The study concludes that strengthening institutional support, improving communication between stakeholders, expanding access to finance and infrastructure, and aligning empowerment initiatives with industry needs are essential to enhancing SMME sustainability and supporting inclusive workforce development. The study contributes to the growing body of knowledge on SMME empowerment by demonstrating the close relationship between enterprise development, youth employability, and regional workforce development within South Africa's automotive industry.

items.title: Exploring the role of green innovation and logistics in linking Logistics 4.0 to sustainable performance: why digitalisation alone is not enough?
items.abstract: The logistics sector operates as a complex sociotechnical system in which digital transformation and environmental sustainability interact as interdependent subsystems. Logistics 4.0 technologies are credited with improving operational efficiency, yet how they translate into performance remains underexplored within an integrated systems framework. Drawing on a systems science perspective, this study examines how Logistics 4.0 affects logistics performance directly and indirectly through green logistics and green innovation. Survey data from 338 manufacturing firms were analysed using structural equation modelling and mediation analysis. All seven hypothesised relationships were supported: Logistics 4.0 predicted green logistics (β = 0.735), green innovation (β = 0.631) and performance (β = 0.532), and both mediators predicted performance (β = 0.647 and 0.419). The mediating channels differ in magnitude: green logistics carries a strong indirect effect (k2 = 0.331) and green innovation a moderate one (k2 = 0.203), indicating that the operational and strategic routes to sustainable performance mature on different horizons. The study contributes by modelling these constructs as complementary subsystems rather than isolated variables, and by differentiating empirically the strength of the two mediating channels. For managers and policymakers, the implication is direct: digitalisation delivers its full return only when planned jointly with sustainability capability.

items.title: Extended Judgment: LLMs and the Architecture of Artificial Capacities
items.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly embedded in everyday epistemic practices, yet their epistemological status remains unclear. Existing debates typically oscillate between treating LLMs as epistemic agents or reducing them to mere tools. This paper argues that both views mischaracterize the core issue. Drawing on a teleological interpretation of 4E cognition and the paradigm of human–AI coevolution, it develops an alternative account that understands LLMs as components of extended epistemic capacities, most centrally the human capacity for judgment. On this view, epistemic capacities are not intrinsic properties of isolated subjects or systems, but purposive and relational achievements enacted within sociotechnical practices. LLMs do not possess epistemic agency or original normativity; rather, they reshape the conditions under which human judgment, inquiry, understanding, and justification unfold. By analyzing language, coevolutionary feedback loops, derived normativity, and epistemic autonomy, the paper shows how epistemic responsibility remains human while epistemic performance becomes technologically extended.
